**ID:** SN 34

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Structurally, the collection is constructed as a comprehensive combinatorial "wheel" (*cakka*) that pairs meditative skills dyadically across all possibilities [Bodhi 2003; Bodhi 2003_x]. Each pair of qualities is analyzed through a fourfold matrix: a practitioner who possesses the first skill but not the second, one who possesses the second but not the first, one who possesses neither, and one who possesses both [Bodhi 2003_x]. In every discourse, the meditator who has perfected both skills is pronounced the foremost and most excellent [Bodhi 2003_x]. The text is commented upon in the *Sāratthappakāsinī* (Spk), the commentary to the *Saṁyuttanikāya* [Bodhi 2003_x].

 In addition, DharmaNexus records extensive internal Pali text reuse across 75 texts, showing the highest volume of shared formulaic phrasing with the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51), and the Abhidhamma's *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* (Vb 16) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages automatically with Tibetan canonical texts, such as the *Kalāpasūtravṛtti* (D4288) and Prajñāpāramitā treatises (D3787, D3807) [DharmaNexus].
